paper.title: Best-item Learning in Random Utility Models with Subset Choices

settings.name_in_paper: (epsilon,delta)-PAC best item identification in RUM(k,theta) with winner (WI) feedback
unmapped: Learner plays a subset of exactly k_sub items per round and observes the winner drawn from a random utility model X_i = theta_i + zeta_i with iid noise zeta_i ~ D (general noise distribution with density)
The learner knows the noise-dependent constant c (lower bound on the sensitivity of the minimum advantage ratio) and the subset size k_sub
settings.definition_quote: At each decision round $t = 1, 2, \ldots$, the learner selects a subset $S_t \subseteq [n]$ of $k$ distinct items, and receives (stochastic) feedback depending on (a) the chosen subset $S_t$, and (b) a \rumk\, choice model ... Winner of the selected subset (WI): The environment returns a single item $I \in S$, drawn independently from the probability distribution $Pr(I = i|S) = Pr(X_i > X_j, ~\forall j \in S\sm \{i\} )$

settings.name_in_paper: (epsilon,delta)-PAC best item identification in RUM(k,theta) with top-m ranking (TR-m) feedback
unmapped: Learner plays a subset of exactly k_sub items per round and observes the top-m_top ranking of the subset under a random utility model with iid noise
The learner knows the noise-dependent constant c, the subset size k_sub and m_top
settings.definition_quote: Top-$m$ ranking of items (TR-$m$): In this feedback setting, the environment is assumed to return a ranking of only $m$ items from among $S$, i.e., the environment first draws a full ranking $\bsigma$ over $S$ according to \rumk\, as in FR above, and returns the first $m$ rank elements of $\bsigma$

algorithms.name: mSeq-PB (Sequential-Pairwise-Battle with top-m ranking feedback and rank breaking)

symbols.k_sub: subset size k played each round

conditions: iid noise RUM: X_i = theta_i + zeta_i, zeta_i ~ D iid with density
Min-AR(i,j) >= 1 + 4c*Delta_ij/(1-2c) for every item pair, for some D-dependent c > 0
tuning: epsilon_0 = c*epsilon/8, delta_0 = delta/2, epsilon_l = 3/4 epsilon_{l-1}, delta_l = delta_{l-1}/2

source.label: thm:alg_pp
source.quote: Consider any iid subsetwise preference model \rumk\, based on a noise distribution $\cD$, and suppose that for any item pair $i,j$, we have \mrat$(i,j) \ge 1 + \frac{4c\Delta_{ij}}{1-2c}$ for some $\cD$-dependent constant $c > 0$. Then, Algorithm \ref{alg:pp}, with input constant $c > 0$, is an $(\epsilon,\delta)$-{PAC} algorithm with sample complexity $O(\frac{n}{c^2\epsilon^2} \log \frac{k}{\delta})$.

results.notes: Paper's n (number of items) mapped to K. The algorithm's number of rounds is deterministic; recorded as expectation per paper's definition of sample complexity. Also yields (epsilon,delta)-PAC correctness.

symbols.k_sub: subset size k played each round

conditions: noise distribution D is one of Exponential(1), Gumbel(mu,sigma), Gamma(2,1), Uniform(a,b), Weibull(lambda,1), Normal(0,1)
tuning: c set to the distribution-specific constant (e.g. 0.25 for Exponential(1), 1/3 for N(0,1))

source.label: cor:alg_pp
source.quote: For the following representative noise distributions: Exponential$(1)$, Gumbel$(\mu,\sigma)$ Gamma$(2,1)$, Uniform$(a,b)$, Weibull$(\lambda,1)$, Standard normal or Normal$(0,1)$, \algp\, (Alg.\ref{alg:pp}) finds an $(\epsilon,\delta)$-{PAC} item within sample complexity $O\big( \frac{n}{\epsilon^2}\ln \frac{k}{\delta} \big)$.

results.notes: Special case of Theorem thm:alg_pp with c constant; for Gumbel/Uniform/Weibull c depends on sigma, b-a, lambda which are absorbed into the O. Normal case relies on a small-gap approximation.

symbols.c: constant with Min-AR(i,j) >= 1 + 4c Delta_ij on the hard instance

conditions: for any (epsilon,delta)-PAC algorithm with winner item feedback
there exists a RUM(k,theta) instance with Min-AR(i,j) >= 1 + 4c*Delta_ij for all i,j

source.label: thm:lb_pacpl_win
source.quote: Given $\epsilon \in (0,\frac{1}{4}]$, $\delta \in (0,1]$, $c > 0$  and an $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC algorithm $A$ with winner item feedback, there exists a \rumk\, instance $\nu$ with \mrat$(i,j) \ge 1 + 4c\Delta_{ij}$ for all $i,j \in [n]$, where the expected sample complexity of $A$ on $\nu$ is  at least $\Omega\big( \frac{n}{c^2\epsilon^2} \ln \frac{1}{2.4\delta}\big)$.

results.notes: Proof yields (n-1)/(128 c^2 eps^2) ln(1/(2.4 delta)) with c = 1/4 fixed by the Gumbel construction.

symbols.k_sub: subset size k played each round
symbols.m_top: length m of the top-m ranking feedback

conditions: iid noise RUM with noise distribution D
Min-AR(i,j) >= 1 + 4c*Delta_ij/(1-2c) for every item pair, for some D-dependent c > 0
tuning: t = ceil(4k/(m eps_l^2) ln(2k/delta_l)) plays per group

source.label: thm:alg_ppm
source.quote: Consider any \rumk\, subsetwise preference model based on noise distribution $\cD$ and suppose for any item pair $i,j$,  we have \mrat$(i,j) \ge 1 + \frac{4c\Delta_{ij}}{1-2c}$ for some $\cD$-dependent constant $c > 0$. Then \algpm\, (Alg.\ref{alg:ppm}) with input constant $c > 0$ on top-$m$ ranking feedback model is an $(\epsilon,\delta)$-{PAC} algorithm with sample complexity $O(\frac{n}{mc^2\epsilon^2} \log \frac{k}{\delta})$.

results.notes: Paper's n mapped to K, paper's k to k_sub, paper's m to m_top.

symbols.m_top: length m of the top-m ranking feedback
symbols.c: constant with Min-AR(i,j) >= 1 + 4c Delta_ij on the hard instance

conditions: there exists a RUM(k,theta) instance with Min-AR(i,j) >= 1 + 4c*Delta_ij for all i,j

source.label: thm:lb_pacpl_rank
source.quote: Given $\epsilon \in (0,\frac{1}{4}]$ and $\delta \in (0,1]$, and an $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC algorithm $A$ with winner item feedback, there exists a \rumk\, instance $\nu$, in which for any pair $i,j \in [n]$ \mrat$(i,j) \ge 1 + 4c\Delta_{ij}$, where the expected sample complexity of $A$ on $\nu$ with top-$m$ ranking feedback has to be at least $\Omega\bigg( \frac{n}{mc^2\epsilon^2} \ln \frac{1}{2.4\delta}\bigg)$ for A to be $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC.

results.notes: Proof only sketched (KL chain rule giving m-factor). Statement says 'winner item feedback' but bound is for top-m feedback.
